questions: Are these movements in your arms and hands involuntary and hard to control?
Did these movements start in the past few days or weeks?
Do you feel pain in your arms, hands, or joints when you have these movements?
Have you taken any new prescription medications recently before these began?
Do these movements get worse when you feel stressed or anxious?
Have you had a head injury or spinal injury in the past?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hands or arms?
Is there a family history of similar involuntary movements?
Have you been exposed to any chemicals, poisons, or heavy metals recently?
Do these movements stop when you sleep or when you try to consciously suppress them?
results: 1. tremor frequency estimate: slow, under about 4.5 Hz, with a wing-beating quality
2. brain MRI: thalamic lesion (tuberculoma) that DECREASED in size after anti-tuberculous treatment, with no gliosis
3. tuberculosis treatment history: CNS tuberculoma treated with anti-tuberculous therapy; the tremor began after treatment was completed
dx_raw: DIAGNOSIS: Rubral tremor secondary to thalamic tuberculoma (sequelae of CNS tuberculosis)
dx: Rubral tremor secondary to thalamic tuberculoma (sequelae of CNS tuberculosis)
